column1: # synui-plugins browse — widgets you can install, and where they come from.
# ⚠ EVERY ROW HERE HAS BEEN LOADED INTO A REAL BAR, not merely read. A catalogue
# that lists a widget which turns out to need Hyprland, or a component this
# desktop does not implement, is a catalogue that installs disappointments — so
# a row is added only after the widget has been through tests/plugin_load.sh's
# path. Omarchy's KeyboardLayout and Workspaces are deliberately absent: both
# import Quickshell.Hyprland and would be refused at install time. Their Tray
# needs a PopupCard this desktop does not have, and SynapseOS has its own tray.
# ⚠ THE MANIFEST IS NAMED <Base>.manifest.json IN THEIR TREE, not manifest.json.
# Their bar widgets share one directory, so each carries its own; a standalone
# plugin has the plain name. The installer renames on the way in, which is the
# one shape difference between "a widget in Omarchy's repo" and "a plugin".
# ⚠ TWELVE COLUMNS, AND THE REGISTRY CACHE HAS THE SAME TWELVE. This file is
# the hand-tested floor of a list that is mostly fetched: `synui-plugins
# refresh` writes ~/.cache/synui/plugins/registry.tsv in this exact shape out of
# omarchyplugins.com, and every browser reads the two concatenated. One format,
# so a row is a row wherever it came from.
# `path` and `base` name one widget inside a repository that holds many, which
# is what these rows are and what the sparse checkout below fetches. A registry
# row leaves both EMPTY: its repository IS the plugin, and the install is a
# plain clone.
# `trust` is `shipped` here and only here. It means the widget was loaded into a
# real synui bar before the row was written. The registry's own `verified` is a
# different claim by different people about a different desktop, and collapsing
# the two into one badge would be the browser telling a lie it cannot back.
# id <TAB> name <TAB> description <TAB> repo <TAB> ref <TAB> path <TAB> base
#    <TAB> category <TAB> tags <TAB> author <TAB> stars <TAB> trust
